newsitem.title: USA: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DALLAS CLINCHES NFC EAST, REDSKINS ELIMINATED FROM PLAYOFFS.
newsitem.headline: NFL AMERICAN FOOTBALL-DALLAS CLINCHES NFC EAST, REDSKINS ELIMINATED FROM PLAYOFFS.

text.p: Chris Boniol kicked four field goals to lead the Dallas Cowboys to a 12-6 victory over the New England Patriots on Sunday that clinched their fifth successive NFC East Division title.
The win was the third in a row and fifth in six games for the Cowboys (10-5), who overcame a 1-3 start.

"Winning five division titles in a row is nice, I congratulated our players," said Switzer, who steered the Cowboys to their last three division crowns. "But all it really does is get you in position to attain your final goal."
The loss denied New England (10-5) a chance to claim the AFC East title. The Pats, already in the playoffs, can still win the division crown if Buffalo loses Monday at Miami.
New England entered the game as the NFL's top-scoring team with 389 points, but failed to reach the end zone against Dallas' number one ranked defence.
At Arizona, Kevin Butler's 28-yard field goal as time expired gave the Arizona Cardinals a 27-26 victory over Washington, knocking the Redskins out of playoff contention despite a 7-1 start.
Butler beat the Redskins (8-7) for the second time this season. His 32-yard field goal with 33 seconds left in overtime gave Arizona a 37-34 win at Washington last month.
Sunday's kick capped a 15-play, 69-yard drive that consumed the final 7:14 as Kent Graham, starting for the first time since November 3, directed the winning drive.
Gus Frerotte was 20-for-42 for 258 yards for the Redskins (8-7), who have lost three straight and six of the last seven.
The Redskins loss set the NFC playoffs field -- Green Bay, Carolina, San Francisco, Dallas, Minnesota and Philadelphia.

In Pittsburgh, Steve Young threw for 253 yards and three touchdowns and the San Francisco 49ers had a safety and forced two key turnovers in a 25-15 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers, who had a 13-game home winning streak snapped.

Jerry Rice caught eight passes for 63 yards and a touchdown and became the first NFL receiver with three consecutive 100-catch seasons for the 49ers (11-4), who have clinched a playoff berth but are still jockeying with Carolina for the NFC West title and a possible first-round bye.
"A heck of a lot better than last week," said 49ers coach George Seifert, referring to a home loss to Carolina.
Pittsburgh (10-5) already has clinched the AFC Central Division but also is playing for a possible first-round bye.

At Carolina, Kerry Collins threw a pair of second-half touchdown passes and the second-year Carolina Panthers moved within one victory of the NFC West title with their sixth straight win, 27-16 over the Baltimore Ravens.

The Panthers (11-4) and San Francisco 49ers own identical records, but Carolina swept the season series from the Niners and holds the tie-breaker. Carolina, the first team ever to clinch a playoff berth in their second year, can claim the division crown with a victory over Pittsburgh next Sunday.

"Many people wondered if our team would be able to come out and play at a high level after an emotional win at San Francisco last week," Carolina coach Dom Capers said. "Our team showed maturity in all our preparation."

At Minnesota, Leroy Hoard rushed for 101 yards and two touchdowns and Brad Johnson hit Cris Carter with a 36-yard scoring pass to lead the Minnesota Vikings to their third straight win, a 21-10 victory over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
The Vikings (9-6) avenged a 24-13 loss at Tampa Bay two months ago. The Buccaneers dropped to 5-10.
In Detroit, Brett Favre passed for a touchdown and ran for another and Desmond Howard scored on a 92-yard punt return to lead the Green Bay Packers to a 31-3 rout of the Lions.
The win clinched a first-round playoff bye for the Packers (12-3), who can clinch home-field advantage throughout the playoffs with a win against Minnesota next Sunday.
Favre threw his league-leading 36th touchdown pass early in the fourth quarter, a 27-yard toss to Antonio Freeman.
The Lions (5-10) dropped their fourth straight.

In Denver, Aaron Craver ran for one score and John Elway had a touchdown pass to Rod Smith during a 17-point second quarter as the Broncos survived a late rally and eliminated the Oakland Raiders from playoff contention with a 24-19 win.
Denver (13-2), which owns the best record in the NFL, finished its home schedule with a perfect 8-0 record. Oakland (7-8) had its three-game winning streak snapped.
Oakland was penalised 20 times, the highest-single game total since Tampa Bay against Seattle in 1976, for 157 yards.

In Kansas City, Jim Harbaugh, playing for the first time in three weeks, threw three touchdown passes to rookie Marvin Harrison as the Indianapolis Colts remained in the playoff hunt with a 24-19 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs.
Harbaugh completed 16-of-28 passes for 227 yards without an interception. He had missed the last two games -- both wins -- with a knee injury.
Both teams have 9-6 records.

In Houston, James Hundon's first NFL catch -- a 14-yard touchdown reception from Jeff Blake with 4:34 left in the third quarter -- put the Cincinnati Bengals ahead for good in a 21-13 victory over the Houston Oilers.
Before the game, the Bengals gave Bruce Coslet a four-year contract to stay on as head coach. Coslet took over for David Shula on October 1 and the Bengals have gone 6-2 since.
The Oilers and Bengals, both 7-8, were eliminated from playoff contention.
In other games, St Louis beat Atlanta 34-27 and the New Orleans embarrassed the hosting New York Giants 17-3.

In Jacksonville, Mark Brunell threw two TD passes to Jimmy Smith, including a 39-yarder on the first play of the fourth quarter, as the Jaguars stayed alive in the playoff hunt with a come-from-behind 20-13 win over the Seattle Seahawks.
Jacksonville (8-7) has won four straight to move within a game of the Kansas City Chiefs and Indianapolis Colts in the chase for the last two AFC playoff spots.
Buffalo (9-5), also looking to wrap up a playoff berth, visits Miami Monday night. Jacksonville ends its season against Atlanta next week.
